newsitem.title: USA: Leach presses Freddie, Fannie on plans.
newsitem.headline: Leach presses Freddie, Fannie on plans.

text.p: House Banking Committee chairman Rep Jim Leach on Thursday called for the Clinton administration to review new programs adopted by three government-sponsored entities.

The Iowa Republican said Housing and Community Development Secretary Andrew Cuomo should examine new initiatives at Federal National Mortgage Association, Freddie Mac and the Federal Home Loan Bank System.
"In each case, they have sought unilaterally to expand their authority," Leach said in a letter to Cuomo.

"From the perspective of protecting a market economy as well as management of public debt, I believe it is essential that the executive branch establish a coherent inter-agency framework by which proposed new programs and activities of these GSEs are reviewed," Leach wrote.

Leach asked for a review of Fannie Mae's new program called the Mortgage Protection Plan, Freddie Mac's decision to build a $10 billion inventory of non-housing related long-term investments and loan participation programs at the Chicago and New York Federal Home Loan Banks.
Officials at HUD, Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac and the Office of Federal Housing Enterprise Oversight were not immediately available for comment.

"The key from a public perspective is to insist that management's eyes remain focused on their housing mission, not on tangential areas which appear primarily aimed at stockholder returns, not public purpose," Leach said in his letter.
